description: Dark hide split at the shoulders and spine, lit bone standing up through it. You see one coming a long way off.
lore: On all fours, hunched, with long arms and hands that end in fingers rather than paws, and quicker on that hunch than a thing built like that has any right to be. The hide is dark and split: along the shoulders, down the whole length of the spine, at the flanks. Standing up through the splits is bone, pale, carrying its own light. The head is bone the whole way round, two sockets in it and nothing you can find in them that is looking back.

Everything else out in that country is at some stage of going. A shape with the details gone but the round still walked. A shape with nothing left in it but the last thing it ever learned. Then, in its own time, nothing. This one is at no stage at all. It did not get here the slow way; it went into the ground one way and came out the other, and where the long accounting ought to be there is a light instead, and the light has not gone down by so much as a shade.

Keepers who worked the eastern circuit used to say there was one mercy left near the mouth and this was it, a thing that cannot cross a black wood without announcing itself. They stopped saying it after somebody watched one hunt. The light is not leaking and it is not for your benefit. It comes up out of the ribs at whatever is standing close in front, and anything that has been in an unlit place long enough to have given up on light goes blind where it stands and is still standing there, blind, when the long raking arm arrives. The crouch, the reach, the arm — all of it is built for coming out of the dark, and the light is the part that does the work.

Bone is all that comes off it, and nothing stranger than bone: ribs bleached clean, hooked talons in matched sets, some of them the same grey hooks the horned fiends shed, a marrow bone knobbed at both ends and stained where beige should not be. It bleeds, too, and freely, which is not what people expect from something that was emptied. Breaking it goes wrong in a particular way. It comes apart at the neck, the lit head leaves first, and the rest of it stays up on its hands a moment afterwards, which is the part that anyone who has seen it gets to in the telling and then skips. The hard piece is dark and banded, with a seam of live gold in it that has not gone out and is not going to, warm, and impossible to forget. It is the same light that was in the bones: in a weapon it burns what it touches, and close in it does to other things exactly what the ribs did. That light was burning in there the whole time it was out in that country. It was never once lit for anybody.
